findings.title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false despite appearing conditional
Unsafe SQL formatting pattern retained as dead code
findings.body: `TablesList` still constructs a SQL command with `fmt.Sprintf("SELECT json_serialize_sql('%s')", rawSQL)` after only escaping single quotes. Although the new stub DB returns `"not implemented"` before any statement is actually evaluated, the vulnerable code path is still reachable via `UnmarshalSQLCommand` / `NewSQLCommand`, which are not gated by the new `enableSqlExpressions` check in `reader.go`. More importantly, this retains the exact pattern that made CVE-2024-9264 exploitable; if anyone later restores DuckDB to "re-enable" SQL expressions, the injection re-emerges immediately. Since `TablesList` now always returns the stub error and is never useful, the entire function (and the unsafe `Sprintf`/`Replace`/`RunCommands` calls) should be deleted rather than preserved in a half-disabled form.

findings.title: Error message claims SQL expressions were never implemented
findings.body: When `enableSqlExpressions` returns false, the reader returns `fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented")`. This message is misleading for two reasons: (a) SQL expressions were shipped and used in dashboards before this PR, so users with existing panels will hit this error and have no way to understand why a previously working feature now fails; (b) the message obscures the actual reason — a security fix for CVE-2024-9264. The error should at minimum mention that the feature has been disabled for security reasons and link to the blog post / release notes, so dashboards that previously used SQL expressions don't silently look like an unimplemented feature. The same misleading message would also be surfaced from `UnmarshalSQLCommand` if `sql.TablesList` is reached.

findings.title: Stub DB has no explanation that this is a CVE-2024-9264 mitigation
findings.body: `pkg/expr/sql/db.go` introduces an empty `DB` struct whose three methods all return `errors.New("not implemented")`, and is wired into `parser.go` and `sql_command.go`. There is no package- or type-level comment explaining that this file exists solely as a CVE-2024-9264 mitigation, that callers must gate usage through `enableSqlExpressions`, or that the methods are deliberately inert. Future maintainers may reasonably assume this is a working SQL backend and try to fill in the methods to re-enable the feature, reintroducing the vulnerability. Add a comment such as `// Stub DB used after CVE-2024-9264 to make SQL expressions return errors; do not implement.`

findings.title: No regression test that SQL expressions are rejected
findings.body: This is a security-driven removal of a feature, but the diff contains no test changes. Existing tests for `ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery` (and for `UnmarshalSQLCommand`) will continue to pass only if they don't exercise the `QueryTypeSQL` branch; there is nothing pinning the new behavior. At minimum, add a test that asserts (a) `ReadQuery` with `QueryTypeSQL` returns an error mentioning SQL expressions are disabled, and (b) `UnmarshalSQLCommand` / `NewSQLCommand` rejects any input. Without this, a future refactor could silently re-enable SQL expressions (e.g. by "simplifying" `enableSqlExpressions`) and re-open CVE-2024-9264.
